summary: Ronald Morton Smith was an Indologist educated at St Andrews, Oxford, and Cambridge. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge (1948–1955), Assistant Professor at Toronto (1955–1982), and chairman at Harvard (1976–1978).

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Calgary (~1977–2007), serving as Associate Professor in Religious Studies (attested 1986) and becoming Professor Emeritus around 2007.

Ronald S. Green works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at UNC Charlotte, Virginia Tech, Oregon, and Wisconsin-Madison, he served at Wisconsin-Madison (2000–2003), Coastal Carolina University (attested 2013), and ASIANetwork (2020–2025).

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1975–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and served on the faculty at Yenching University (~1926–1941).

Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, later holding appointments at McGill and the Center for Chinese Studies.

Ronit Ricci works in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1990–1999) and held posts at the Australian National University (2010) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2014).

Ronit Yoeli-Tlalim works in history/archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at SOAS (1998–2004) and held posts at University College London (attested 2010) and Goldsmiths, University of London, as Professor (2023–2024).

Roper Lethbridge was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Exeter College (~1859–1864), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1881) and was a Fellow of the University of Calcutta (~1877).
Rory Brendan Lindsay specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey and taught at International Christian College.

Rosalind Lefeber is an Indologist who completed her doctoral dissertation at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, also studying under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held an affiliation there (attested 2007).

Rosalind O'Hanlon is an Indology and history scholar who earned her PhD at SOAS (~1976–1982). She held posts at Clare College (~1983) and the University of Oxford (~2004–2021), where she became Professor in Indian History and Culture.

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied and taught at Komazawa University, rising from assistant (1969) to professor (1983–2012). He was also director of the Soto Zen Research Center (2009).

Rosane Rocher is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles and under Ludo Rocher. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970) and became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1970.

Rosemarie Fuchs is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche. She was a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg. She held professorships at the universities of Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and served as president of the Indogermanische Gesellschaft (2004–2016).
Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1959–1965) and held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).

Rosina Pastore is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned degrees from Naples and Lausanne. She held a teaching and research post at Lausanne (2016–2022) and became an affiliated researcher at Ghent University (2022–2025).
Ross Arthur Leslie Moore was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Dulwich College and Peterhouse, Cambridge, where he later served as Lecturer in Marathi (1921–1927).
